slides.title: Alphabet & Sounds
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 1 English, Unit 0: Alphabet & Sounds. You will meet all the letters of the alphabet — big letters and small letters — and learn the sound each one makes. You will trace letters, say their sounds, and blend them into your first little words like cat and sun. You will also learn your first sight words and read tiny sentences. Take your time: knowing your letters well matters more than going fast. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Recognise and name uppercase and lowercase letters.
Connect letters a-z with their most common sounds.
Hear and say beginning sounds in familiar words.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to recognise and name uppercase and lowercase letters. You will also connect letters a-z with their most common sounds. You will also hear and say beginning sounds in familiar words. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: apple, ball, cat, dog, elephant, fish. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Week 1: Learn the Alphabet (A–Z) and Week 2: Phonics (Letter Sounds a–m). Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: The letter A says aaa
bullets: Say the aaa sound, not the letter name. Open your mouth wide, like Sami saying a-a-apple.
slides.narration: The first language focus is The letter A says aaa. Say the aaa sound, not the letter name. Open your mouth wide, like Sami saying a-a-apple. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Sound and say 1. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
